Definition: from G1537 and G190; to follow out, i.e. (figuratively) to imitate, obey, yield to:--follow.
BiblicalUsage: In the New Testament, exakolouthéō is the word for follow. In 2 Peter 1:16, the text says "For we have not followed cunningly devised fables." In 2 Peter 2:2, the text says "And many shall follow their pernicious ways."
TheologicalSignificance: Reading exakolouthéō this way, I believe obedience is not drudgery; it is trusting that God's way is the good way. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
